    Coldspeople¶

    A humanoid mammalian race adapted to extreme cold. Coldspeople prefer to live near ice, in tundra, and in near-permafrost regions — climates that would kill other humanoid species within hours. They are found primarily on Marti Continent, with smaller populations in the northern reaches of Lumina and the high-altitude regions of Xeti.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: Stocky, broad-shouldered, with thick pale fur covering their bodies — white, cream, or light gray. Round faces with small ears (to minimize heat loss). Their hands are paw-like with retractable claws for gripping ice. Eyes are small and dark — adapted for the blinding glare of snow-reflected sunlight.
    • Lifespan: 65–80 years. Coldspeople age slowly in cold environments but rapidly in warm ones — a Coldsperson who moves to a temperate climate may lose a decade of lifespan to metabolic stress.
    • Mage-cell expression: Low — some ice-shaping abilities. Coldsperson mages (called Frost-Singers) can freeze water, create ice walls, and walk on snow without leaving tracks. Combat magic is rare — most Frost-Singers are builders, using ice-shaping to construct and maintain settlements.
    • Adaptation: Thick layer of insulating fat (2–3 inches) and dense fur. Coldspeople can sleep in snow without harm — their body temperature regulation is the most efficient of any known species. Blood runs thicker, heart beats slower, metabolism conserves every calorie. Heat is their vulnerability — they struggle in temperatures above freezing and can suffer heatstroke at temperatures humans find comfortable. A Coldsperson in summer clothing in a temperate room is equivalent to a human in a sauna.

    Society¶

    Coldspeople live in ice-carved settlements — homes sculpted from packed snow and glacial ice, insulated with furs and heated by geothermal vents or carefully contained fire-pits. Their architecture is temporary by design — settlements are carved fresh each winter and allowed to melt each spring, only to be rebuilt the following year.

    • Nations: Brase and communities in Maboro on Marti Continent. Smaller enclaves exist in northern Lumina and high Xeti.
    • Governance: Council of Elders — the oldest living Coldsperson in each settlement leads. Age is wisdom; the eldest have survived the most winters and therefore know the most about survival. Disputes are settled by the eldest who is not personally involved — their word is final.
    • Social structure: Highly communal. Survival in the cold demands cooperation. Food, shelter, and warmth are shared without question. A Coldsperson who hoards resources is not punished — they are pitied. Hoarding means you do not trust your community, and a Coldsperson without community will not survive the winter.
    • Family: Coldspeople raise children collectively. A child belongs to the settlement, not to specific parents. This does not mean parents are absent — it means every adult is a parent. A child who scrapes their knee will be comforted by the nearest adult, regardless of blood relation.

    Culture¶

    Coldsperson culture is shaped by the fundamental reality of their environment: the cold does not care about your feelings. You cooperate or you die. This breeds a culture that is warm internally and cold externally — Coldspeople are famously stoic with outsiders and warmly affectionate with their own.

    • The Winter-Telling: During the deepest part of winter, when blizzards trap settlements for weeks, Coldspeople gather in the communal hall for the Winter-Telling — a continuous storytelling tradition that can last the entire season. Elders tell the old stories. Children learn their history. Travelers who happen to be snowed in are honored guests — they are expected to contribute their own stories in exchange for shelter.
    • Gift-Giving: When a Coldsperson visits another settlement, they bring a gift of food — typically preserved meat or frozen berries. The gift is not optional. It is a statement: "I come in peace, I contribute to your survival, I am not a burden." To arrive without a gift is an insult. To refuse a gift is a declaration of hostility.
    • Relations: Trade furs, ice-gems, and preserved meat with Germina and the Cobal Kingdom. Neutral toward most species. Wary of outsiders who do not understand their customs — the gift-giving ritual has caused diplomatic incidents when human traders arrived empty-handed.
    • Death: When a Coldsperson dies, their body is placed on a funeral pyre of scented wood (imported at great expense). The fire is lit at dusk. The community watches the smoke rise into the frozen night. They believe the soul rises with the smoke to join the Great Cold — the eternal winter where ancestors dwell. Bodies are never buried — the frozen ground is too hard, and burial would trap the soul in the earth.

    Religion — Ulasm¶

    Most Coldspeople follow Ulasm — the pagan animist faith that worships eagles as divine and venerates ancestors. The dead dwell in the Great Cold and watch through eagle eyes. Core in Brase (southwest of Germina), also in Coldspeople enclaves in Maboro.

    Ulasm predates the Erisian Church on Marti by millennia; its eagle-feather talismans and dusk pyres remain the heart of Coldspeople spirituality.

    Connections¶

    • Nations: Brase, Maboro (Marti Continent)
    • Enclaves: Northern Lumina, high-altitude Xeti
    • Traits: Cold-adapted, fur-covered, ice-carving, communal, gift-culture
    • Ages: Present since Age 3 in Marti, expanded during Age 7 trade era
